component.name: Kawaro
كوارو
component.summary: Convert files locally from your file manager
حوّل الملفات محلياً من مدير الملفات

description.p: Kawaro converts and processes files entirely on your computer. Select files in your file manager, choose Kawaro from the context menu, and a honeycomb of actions that fit the selected files appears. The result is saved as a new file next to the original.
يحوّل كوارو الملفات ويعالجها على جهازك بالكامل. حدد الملفات في مدير الملفات واختر كوارو من قائمة النقر اليمين، فتظهر خلية نحل بالإجراءات المناسبة لها، ويُحفظ الناتج ملفاً جديداً بجانب الأصل.
No file ever leaves your computer.

Upgrading the Windows MSI from 0.4.0 or 0.4.2 now works (it failed with error 1603). The update page shows the download percent, reopens after the restart with the result, and shows a plain message with a retry when an update fails. On Linux, Alt followed by a late drag now shows the hive. Known limits: the settings window can open behind another window after an update on Windows, and the Windows files are still self-signed, so SmartScreen or Defender may warn.

Urgent Windows fix: upgrading from an older version with the MSI, or with the in-app update, removed the program files and left a broken Start shortcut. If you installed 0.4.1 on Windows, run the 0.4.2 MSI once (or reinstall). A fresh install of 0.4.1 was fine.

A new Settings window with a header, a page rail and an Updates page (installed version, check for updates, update now, automatic check, channel and install mode), plus a simpler website and README. The Windows files are still test-signed with a self-signed certificate, so SmartScreen warns.

The first official release for Linux and Windows. In-app updates, the Windows zip and MSI, the Explorer right click menu, the right-button drag trigger, the first-run welcome, and the Windows beta feedback fixes. The Windows files are test-signed with a self-signed certificate, so SmartScreen warns until a trusted certificate signs them.

First public beta for Linux and Windows. In-app updates through a signed manifest, a Windows zip and MSI, and the global shortcut portal follow-ups. Beta software: see the release notes for the known gaps.

On GNOME and KDE the drop shortcut Super+Z registers itself through the system portal, after a one time consent. On KDE with the strictest focus stealing prevention, the hive no longer takes the keyboard without a valid activation token.
The hive plays its opening animation on Hyprland and KDE again, including the drop hive when a drag reveals it.
The drop hive appears only while you drag files that have an action. Holding the key with no drag, or dragging a file no action takes, shows nothing.
Drag a file, hold a key, and drop it on the hive. The hive opens over every window at the pointer on Hyprland and KDE, and as a centred window on GNOME.
Kawaro appears in app launchers and opens its settings.
Video, audio, documents and PDF through FFmpeg, LibreOffice and Ghostscript, a settings window, and focus that works under strict focus policies in GNOME and KDE.
First release: the hive, image conversion, the background service and command line, and file manager integrations.
